title: privatelink-egress-proxy-and-az-aware-subnet-handoff
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in constrained VPCs reported intermittent egress failures when control-plane outbound traffic was routed through shared NAT or proxy appliances. This PR introduces a controlled VPC PrivateLink-based egress proxy for control-plane components plus an AZ-aware subnet handoff that keeps control-plane ENIs in the same AZ as worker subnets to reduce cross-AZ data charges and improve latency. Changes are implemented primarily in Terraform modules and the controlplane Helm chart, with an idempotent upgrade/rollback script and docs. Scope: terraform modules: new privatelink egress module, security-group least-privilege rules, route table propagation guards; ansible/subnet-handoff playbook for on-prem installers; helm: controlplane values to enable headless egress service + readiness for TLS over privatelink; scripts: upgrade/rollback-controlplane.sh which runs a dry-run then applies changes with health checks; docs: detailed migration steps and Rollback playbook. Checklist: [x] implement privatelink egress module and tests (unit + plan) [x] add AZ-aware subnet handoff playbook [x] update controlplane Helm chart values with feature flag [x] add CI smoke test for control-plane egress [x] add documentation and upgrade playbook [x] validate route propagation and SG audit. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless operators opt into the new privatelink_egress=true flag; upgrade script is safe by default (dry-run + canary). Related: Linear ENG-10234 (private control-plane resiliency), ENG-10577 (egress cost regression). See internal design doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/privatelink-egress (internal).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Please tighten SG egress rules - I see a 0.0.0.0/0 fallback in the initial module. We should only allow AWS-managed prefix lists + the proxy ENI range.
Maya Chen: Updated sg-controlplane.tf to reference aws_managed_prefix_list for S3 and ECR and added explicit privatelink ENI CIDR set. Pushed a follow-up commit (c2381b2).
Lina Gomez: Can we add a safety guard to avoid automatic TGW route propagation? If the customer has multiple TGWs this can leak routes between control-plane and data-plane VPCs.

Maya Chen: Added route_propagation_lock variable and explicit aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_association resources only when enable_tgw_propagation=true. Also documented the risk in the migration guide.
Samir Rao: Upgrade script looks good, but add a --no-reboot-mode for on-prem where reboots are disruptive.
Maya Chen: Added --no-reboot flag and an explicit health-check wait loop that gates completion. Also added CI smoke test to validate no-reboot path.
Arjun Patel: Approved after SG tightening and tests green.
release_notes: Introduce optional PrivateLink-based control-plane egress proxy and AZ-aware subnet handoff. Operators can opt-in with privatelink_egress=true; includes upgrade/rollback script and migration docs. Reduces cross-AZ egress and provides least-privilege SGs for control-plane outbound traffic.
notes_for_ops: To enable in an existing deployment: 1) run installer/scripts/upgrade/rollback-controlplane.sh --dry-run and review plan; 2) set privatelink_egress=true in controlplane values and apply; 3) validate control-plane pods have ENIs in target AZs and that Route53 Resolver rules are configured for cross-account DNS forwarding if applicable. Rollback: rerun script with --rollback flag. See installer/docs/privatelink-egress.md for troubleshooting.
risk_summary: Low-medium: default behavior unchanged. Enabling feature modifies VPC routing and SGs; improper configuration can disrupt egress. Migration includes dry-run and health gates. Customers with complex TGW setups should coordinate with network teams.
testing_summary: Unit terraform plan tests added, helm smoke tests added, ansible idempotence validated. Manual canary applied to two internal staging VPCs and observed no regressions in control-plane health metrics over 48h.
post_merge_actions: 1) publish migration doc to customer-facing KB 2) bump module version in registry 3) monitor control-plane egress metrics and alert on >2x baseline egress after rollout
